BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City OPINION NO MAY 14 ATTY. DOMINIQUE JOSE S. PUZON Provincial Legal Officer Province of La Union Dear Atty. Puzon: This has reference to your letter dated January 1 8, 2023 requesting the Department's legal opinion on the following, quoted herein in toto: 1. Where there are prohibited materials considered as the "corpus delicti" in an ordinance, can the sanggunian provide for the destruction thereof premised on the reason that destruction of these paraphernalia shall achieve the very intention of an ordinance. 2. Whether the imposition of fine is progressive or cumulative. The LGC prescribes a maximum penalty of P5,OOO.00 which the SP may impose. If, for example, the ordinance punishes an act which may be violated more than once in a single occasion, can the ordinance provide that the penalty of P5,000.00 shall be imposed on each count? If so, would it not violate the LGC provision prescribing the P5,OOO.OO maximum imposable penalty allowed for SP? For instance: An ordinance prohibiting schools from not allowing students to march on graduation day. School "A" did not allow 5 students to march in one graduation day. Can a school be penalized the amount P25,000.00 equivalent to P5,OOO.OO fine per student? 3. Where there are ordinances passed by the Congress, Sangguniang Panlalawigan and Sangguniang Bayan penalizing the same prohibited act, which penalty shall be imposed? At the outset, we wish to inform you that the has already been answered by the Department in its Legal Opinion No. 96, s.2021, pertinent portion of which states: Lastly, on the issue regarding the propriety of imposing accessory penalty of confiscation, we likewise answer in the affirmative. It must be noted that the local government units shall exercise the powers which are expressly granted, those necessarily implied therefrom, as well as powers which are necessary, appropriate, or incidental for its efficient and effective governance, and those which are essential to the promotion of the general welfare. Invetably, confiscation of paraphernalia that were used in illegal fishing activities, "Matino, Mahusay, at Maaasahan" Trunkline: (02) 8876-3454

is but necessary and incidental for the efficient and effective implementation of the ordinance. It be could be inferred therefrom that the sanggunian may provide for the destruction or disposal of the confiscated items in the ordinance. However, if the ordinance is an offshoot of national law or policy, the articles or goods that have been confiscated shall be disposed of according to the applicable laws, rules and regulations. On the second query, we are of the view that imposition of fine shall be progressive. If a single act performed on a single occasion resulted in multiple outcomes, such as the scenario in the instant case, we believe that the act must be treated as a single violation of the ordinance. Applying therefore, Section 468(a)(iii)1 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC), one penalty should be imposed for a single violation of the provincial ordinance. As regards third query, we believe that the penalty provided in the ordinance is in conformity with the national law. As a matter of fact, the Supreme Court in the case of People vs. Chong Hong2 has ruled that there is no conflict when an ordinance is enacted to punish an act already punishable under national law. However, it did not specify which law or ordinance should be used against the violator. Our view on the matter is that, it will depend on what particular violation of ordinance is being filed. If it is for violation of a city or municipal ordinance filed with the Metropolitan Trial Courts, Municipal Trial Courts, and Municipal Circuit Trial Courts3 then, the penalty in the municipal ordinance shall be imposed. Otherwise, if the complaint filed is for violation of a provincial ordinance with the Regional Trial Court4, then the penalty in the provincial ordinance shall be imposed. This however, shall be without prejudice to the rule on double jeopardy. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY RITY OF THE SECRETARY: VIC OR R.
